Patrícia, congratulations. I read Karen's performance review. It is one of the best this year.
Thank you, Mark. I also wrote my self-assessment, and honestly, it was a year of big changes.
What was your biggest breakthrough?
Meetings. A year ago I only answered questions. Since then, I have run business reviews and budget calls in English.
And the hardest moment? Every year has a setback.
Harbor Health. If we had talked to their finance team earlier, we would have kept them. That lesson is now a team rule.
That is why this promotion is well-deserved. Going forward, what do you need from us?
Time to keep up my English, and one more step out of my comfort zone: the global conference.
Although it was not easy, it was worth it.
Going forward, I will keep up the practice every week.

Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. I just sent your performance review to Mark, and I wanted to say this by voice, not by email. When you joined my team, you told me that your biggest problem was confidence, not English. You said that you noticed your own mistakes, and that they made you quiet in meetings. This year I have watched you lead calls in the middle of an outage, answer a difficult survey, and tell a CFO the bottom line in one sentence. Your English is not perfect, and nobody's is. But your fluency is strong, and your confidence no longer depends on the day. Keep up the practice, and enjoy the promotion. You earned it.

Hi Patrícia, it is Daniel from Brightwave. Victor told me the news about your promotion, so congratulations from all of us. I want to tell you something that I did not say in the survey. When the sync failed in August, I was ready to look at other vendors. What changed my mind was not the fix. It was your call that same afternoon, when you said: I am not sure yet, but it can't be the server, and I will call you back by five. And you did. Next year we will be opening twenty new stores, and I want you in the kickoff, even if you are a senior manager now. See you in January.
